chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you arrive at Mina, say: O God, this is Mina, which is from the rituals You have bestowed upon us. I ask You to bestow upon me what You bestowed upon Your prophets, for I am Your servant and in Your grasp. Then pray there Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, the late 'Isha, and Fajr. The Imam prays Dhuhr there, and it is not permissible for him to do otherwise, but it is expanded for you to pray with others if you are unable. Then you join them at Arafat.' He said: 'The boundary of Mina is from al-'Aqabah to Wadi Muhassir.'

key_terms.الْعَقَبَةِ: Al-'Aqabah, a landmark defining the boundary of Mina
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the plain where the standing (wuquf) of Hajj takes place
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a sacred site near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj
key_terms.وَادِي مُحَسِّرٍ: Wadi Muhassir, a valley defining the other boundary of Mina

ai.seo_question: What are the specific prayers and supplications prescribed for pilgrims when they arrive at Mina during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific supplication and prayer protocols for pilgrims arriving at Mina, emphasizing the distinction between the Imam’s obligatory single Dhuhr prayer and the pilgrims' flexibility to combine prayers. It underscores the theological significance of Mina as a site of divine favor (*manan*), linking the physical act of pilgrimage to the spiritual legacy of the Prophets. The text also provides precise geographical boundaries for Mina, reflecting the scholarly precision characteristic of Shia fiqh in defining ritual spaces.
